meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Red-shift (physics only), specification section 4.8.2.
final_note: You worked through Red-shift (physics only) — 10 specification statements.

concepts.def: The observed increase in the wavelength of light from most distant galaxies. The light from such a galaxy arrives with a longer wavelength than the same light has when it is produced on Earth, so features in its spectrum appear shifted towards the red end. This effect is called red-shift.

concepts.term: Wavelength and the red end of the spectrum
concepts.def: Wavelength is the distance from one point on a wave to the equivalent point on the next wave. Within the visible spectrum red light has the longest wavelength and violet the shortest, so an increase in wavelength is described as a shift towards the red end of the spectrum. The word red-shift refers to that direction of shift, not to the colour an object appears.

Moving away from the observer. The observed increase in wavelength of light from most distant galaxies is the evidence that those galaxies are receding from us. The faster a galaxy is receding, the bigger the observed increase in the wavelength of its light.

Each element produces its own characteristic pattern of lines in a spectrum, and that pattern can be produced and measured in a laboratory on Earth. When the same pattern is found in light from a distant galaxy, the whole pattern is observed at longer wavelengths, shifted towards the red end. Comparing the two patterns is how the increase in wavelength is observed.

concepts.term: Link between distance, speed and red-shift
concepts.def: The further away the galaxies, the faster they are moving and the bigger the observed increase in wavelength. Distance, recession speed and size of red-shift therefore rise together: a galaxy showing a large red-shift is both further away and moving faster than a galaxy showing a small one.

The observed red-shift provides evidence that space itself (the universe) is expanding. Because every distant galaxy is receding, and recedes faster the further away it is, the galaxies are becoming more widely separated over time. The galaxies are not simply flying outwards through unchanging space away from one special place.

The theory that the universe began from a very small region that was extremely hot and dense. If the universe is expanding now, then in the past everything was closer together, which is what this model describes. The observed red-shift supports the Big Bang theory.

concepts.term: Using observations to arrive at a theory
concepts.def: A scientific theory is an explanation that has to account for what is observed. Scientists observed the red-shift of light from most distant galaxies, and developed the Big Bang theory as a model that explains those observations. When new observations are made, such as those of supernovae from 1998 onwards, the accepted theory has to account for them too, and may be changed.

Since 1998 onwards, observations of supernovae suggest that distant galaxies are receding ever faster. These observations came after the Big Bang theory was already accepted, and they added something the earlier picture did not contain: the recession of distant galaxies is not steady but is speeding up.

Mass in the universe that has not been observed directly. The specification names dark mass as one example of how much about the universe is still not understood, so it is something scientists are aware of but cannot yet fully explain.

The specification names dark energy, alongside dark mass, as an example of something about the universe that is still not understood. Dark mass and dark energy are two different named examples, not two names for one idea, and neither is explained by the Big Bang theory as it currently stands.

mcqs.q: Light from a distant galaxy is compared with light from the same element produced in a laboratory on Earth. What is observed about the light from the galaxy?
options: Its wavelength has increased
Its wavelength has decreased
Its colour has turned red
Its speed has decreased
mcqs.explain: Red-shift is an observed increase in the wavelength of light from most distant galaxies.

mcqs.q: The light from galaxy B shows a bigger observed increase in wavelength than the light from galaxy A. What can be concluded about galaxy B?
options: It is further away than A and moving faster than A
It is closer to us than A and moving faster than A is
It is a larger and brighter galaxy than galaxy A is
It is further away than A and moving slower than A is
mcqs.explain: The further away the galaxies, the faster they are moving and the bigger the observed increase in wavelength.

mcqs.q: The light from most distant galaxies shows red-shift. What does this observation provide evidence for?
options: That galaxies fly outwards through fixed space
That the Earth sits at the centre of everything
That the universe is shrinking back to a point
That space itself (the universe) is expanding
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the observed red-shift is evidence that space itself (the universe) is expanding.

mcqs.q: According to the Big Bang theory, how did the universe begin?
options: As an explosion of matter into a huge space already present
From a very large region that was extremely cold and sparse
From a very small region that was extremely hot and dense
When a very large star collapsed and then blew itself apart
mcqs.explain: This is exactly what the specification says the Big Bang theory suggests.

mcqs.q: What do observations of supernovae made since 1998 onwards suggest about distant galaxies?
options: They are receding from us ever faster
They are receding but are slowing down
They have stopped receding from us
They are now moving back towards us
mcqs.explain: Since 1998 onwards, observations of supernovae suggest that distant galaxies are receding ever faster.

mcqs.q: Every distant galaxy is observed to be receding, and the further away a galaxy is the faster it recedes. Why is this evidence of an expanding universe?
options: We are at the centre of the explosion, so everything else moves away from us
Space itself is stretching, so galaxies separate faster the further apart they are
The galaxies were thrown outwards through space and have never slowed since
The nearest galaxies recede fastest, so the outer edge is being left behind
mcqs.explain: A uniform expansion of space makes every galaxy recede, with the most distant receding fastest.

mcqs.q: How does the observed red-shift provide evidence for the Big Bang model?
options: Galaxies are separating now, so in the past matter was in a far smaller, denser region
Red-shift proves that the Big Bang happened, so no other model can now be tested
The red glow we detect is the flash of the explosion still on its way to us
Red-shift shows the galaxies are burning out, so the universe must have begun
mcqs.explain: Running an expanding universe backwards leads to the very small, extremely hot and dense region the theory describes.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes how scientists were able to use observations to arrive at the Big Bang theory?
options: They decided what the theory should say, then looked for facts that would fit it
They observed the red-shift of distant galaxies and built a theory that explains it
They proved the theory by an experiment, so it can never be altered by anyone
They based the theory on the supernovae observed since 1998 onwards, and no other
mcqs.explain: A theory is developed to account for observations that can be made, and red-shift is that observation.

mcqs.q: Which statement about dark mass and dark energy matches the specification?
options: They are fully explained by the Big Bang theory as it currently stands
They are two different names used by scientists for the very same thing
They are examples of what is still not understood about the universe
They are the dark lines seen in the spectra of the most distant galaxies
mcqs.explain: The specification names them as examples of how much about the universe is not understood.

mcqs.q: The pattern of lines in the spectrum of a distant galaxy is compared with the pattern produced by the same element in a laboratory. The galaxy's lines are all found closer to the red end. What does this show?
options: The wavelength has decreased, so the galaxy is receding from us
The wavelength has increased, so the galaxy is receding from us
The wavelength has increased, so the galaxy is approaching us
The galaxy is made of red-hot gas rather than the element used
mcqs.explain: A shift towards the red end is an increase in wavelength, observed in light from galaxies that are receding.

mcqs.q: Light from galaxies X, Y and Z is examined. X shows a small increase in wavelength, Y a medium increase and Z a large increase. Which galaxy is furthest away, and which is moving fastest?
options: X is furthest away and X is moving fastest
Z is furthest away and X is moving fastest
X is furthest away and Z is moving fastest
Z is furthest away and Z is moving fastest
mcqs.explain: The bigger the observed increase in wavelength, the faster the galaxy moves and the further away it is.

mcqs.q: The supernova observations made since 1998 onwards changed what scientists say about the expansion of the universe. What does this show about scientific theories?
options: Once a theory is accepted new observations cannot alter it
New observations showed the expansion has been slowing down
New observations replaced red-shift as evidence of expansion
New observations can change what an accepted theory says
mcqs.explain: Theories must account for the observations available, so new evidence can revise an accepted model.

mcqs.q: Explain qualitatively why light from a galaxy that is receding is observed with a longer wavelength than the same light produced on Earth.
options: The light slows down on its long journey, so its waves are longer on arrival
The light loses energy in dust in space, which reddens it as a sunset is reddened
The galaxy moves away as the light travels, so the waves reach us stretched out
The galaxy moves away from us, which squashes the waves to a shorter wavelength
mcqs.explain: Recession of the source while the light is emitted increases the observed wavelength; this is red-shift.
